title: Tarkir: Dragonstorm Commander: card flavor text

paragraphs.text: For peace, lead by example.
"We stand or fall as a family. All of us." —Betor
"That's not a dragon. Can't be. It's too small, isn't it?" —Askar, Temur scout, last words
Finding all of the lost Jeskai archives was merely the first step to restoration. Wresting them from their draconic keeper proved much more challenging.
"Remember, wait till they're near the top. We don't just want them gone—we want them demoralized." —Vennra, earthcarver tactician
"You had your warning. Now you get *us*." —Eshki Dragonclaw
Its very presence forces nature to adapt.
"Death is a natural thing. It replenishes the land's energy and nourishes the growth of all life."
When dalkovans need protecting, all respond.
When hearts and minds align, so too do actions.
Without subjects, but a tyrant nonetheless.
"The Jeskai like talking about their Way? Let's see them talk their way out of this dilemma." —Girdah, Abzan beastrider
It's the reason monks gave up on mapping Qadat.
"Blink or don't. You'll get hit either way."
"Many hands make light work! Or two hands and a trunk, as the case may be." —Sanzar, Kin-Tree Warden
"You had your warning. Now you get us." —Eshki Dragonclaw
Younger dragons bow to its will, not out of respect, but out of fear.
"Sleep, and return your energy to the lifepool. Sleep, and enrich the land for the next harvest."
"Remind Zurgo that the Abzan will not tolerate his marauders. If the Mardu wish to trespass, then I encourage him to face my blade himself." —Felothar, khan of the Abzan
"For every problem, a thousand answers. For every answer, a thousand branching consequences."
"Jade-touched, wisteria-crowned, with gifts of gold and the Harvest's blessing, return this honored one to us as sibsig." —Priests' chant
The hydrorats were soon eradicated from the monastery.
"On a good day, I am not Fangkeeper, war hero, or sibsig, but a farmer again." —Kotis, the Fangkeeper
The Kin-Tree of Anafenza Mevak was the first recovered after Dromoka's reign, and it stands as a symbol of the Abzan's revival.
The Jeskai find potential recruits among all walks of life, including other clans.
"What tribute have you for our dragonlord?"
"Beware the spirits that claim knowledge beyond the moon; beware the ritual that summons them." —Edict of the Lunarch Council
After lightning struck the cliffs, the ore became iron, the iron became steel, and the steel became greaves. The lightning never left.
Mardu blacksmiths can distill the technology of any clan and make it their own. Whether or not they should is another question.
Sometimes restoring the lost archives of the Jeskai can be as simple as the quiet ruffle of pages and the smell of fresh ink.
Mardu lightning fences are the ingenious synthesis of blacksmith skill and stormsinger magic, protecting their dalkovans from even the most fearsome dragonstorms.
Safe havens amid the desert and dragonstorms, Abzan fortresses attract merchants, travelers, outcasts, and exiles.
At the general's triumphant return, renewed strength surged through the soldiers' ranks.
The angels appreciated the offer but politely declined to eat any birdseed.
When the earth shudders, the sky overflows.
When a redcap raid threatened the Grand Ball at Delverhaugh, Goddric had no choice but to reveal his true identity and douse the invaders in dragonfire.
"May the memory of our fallen heroes ensnare the violent hearts of lesser men." —Great Threshold of Monserkat inscription
"One faith, but many hands in victory."
The roar of applause drowned out the melee raging in the lobby.
Those who are chosen do not doubt. Those who remain do not lament.

"Odum and Broadbark were the only beings mighty enough to challenge the giant Moran the Destroyer. Their battle lasted a hundred dawns, until Moran became so exhausted that he fell into namesleep. He awoke as Moran the Gardener." —*The Tale of Odum and Broadbark*
The murdered inhabitants of Hollowhenge impart to the living the terror they felt in death.
"Speak little. Do much."
The gods are fascinated by innocence, perhaps because it's a quality they themselves lack.
They charge into battle and out for their morning walk with the same exuberance.
Rhoxes who live long enough to retire from war lend support with their extensive knowledge of combat injuries.
"There is always more to give."
"Cut the beasts out from under them and their strength is nothing." —Vona of Iedo, Butcher of Magan
The assembled partygoers fell silent and stared. As the helmet came to a clattering stop, the only sound was Ash's distant footsteps.
A blazing sun that never sets.
"The arc of my blade has carved a path of light for the peace that will follow."
"Your father was a dear friend to whom I owe much. He wanted me to look after you, to care for you should something happen to him."
Its pulsating cry shatters bonds of iron, granite, and servitude.
"I search for a vision of Zendikar that does not include the Eldrazi." —Expedition journal entry
The lives of elves are long, but their memories are longer. Even after death, they do not desert their homes.
From the moment they arrived, wedding guests were met with a pageant of wealth and excess.
The sky takes flight and the earth trembles.
Some emeritus professors return from their wanderings periodically to share tales of the mystical wonders of Arcavios.
"Get out of my way."
"Four parts molten bronze, yes . . . one part frozen mercury, yes, yes . . . but then what?"
Ivold gasped in surprise. Either a very strange insect had crawled onto one of the lenses or he was seeing geists at last!
Another imminent battle subsided in busy snuffling and carefree rooting.
"No fact escapes me. Why do you think you can?"
The wyrmling studied the ancient carvings and dreamed of a day when her own exploits would be immortalized in stone.
It took the banning of temporal manipulation at Tolaria West to teach its students the value of time.
"I adore your outfit. It's so . . . rustic."
Hedrons perplex minds both great and small.
The pull of the tide star holds eternal sway.
Beneath the waves, lost gods stir in their slumber.
"It's easy to anticipate Captain Storm's orders: take the more dangerous route."
Tomorrow belongs to those who prepare for it today.
Some spellcrafting mistakes go on to become spells of their own.
"From the day we are born, we do our best to survive. We fight. We run. We fear. But we cannot protect ourselves from change." —Ark, lizardfolk blacksmith
The masks float downstream toward the Mirrorlake, where faces arise to wear them.
"Either I know just the spell I need, or I'm about to."
Countless delights drift on the surface while dark schemes run below.
"The awestruck birds gazed at Wonder. Slowly, timidly, they rose into the air." —*Scroll of Beginnings*
Lives taken are lives not easily forgotten.
It does no good to bar the gate when the enemy is already inside.
Though he wept at Inti's death, Caparocti's eyes were keen, and his spear pierced cleanly through Clavileño's tainted heart.
"Keep your distance. It may be broken, but it's far from benign." —Stenn
"That's a pretty ring! Trade you my knife for it."
"Lord Bolas has shown me how each miserable little life holds untold resources."
Open hostilities are strictly forbidden at the Inventors' Fair, but "accidents" still happen.
"On vile wings and bloody wind, the swarm will rise." —Skyclave inscription
Ancient evils dwell within the burning chasm called the Ashmouth, ever ready to devour those foolish enough to travel alone.
"There will be no secrets between us... like it or not."
On Innistrad, one person's windfall usually starts with another person lying face down in the mud.
It shambled from the cloud of ash and bone dust, undeterred by its own extinction.
His spark lost, he plots revenge upon the plane whose corrupting mana fractured his soul.
"There are dark, ancient arts that fascinate even me." —Sorin Markov
Death is no excuse to stop working.
"If none of the bones are original, is it even the same skele—aaagh!" —Mort the Philosopher, last words
No part goes to waste.
"Die. But die knowing that your pathetic life will yield a great bounty for me." —Zul Ashur, lich lord
In matters of life and death, he trusts his gut.
"The time for subtlety is over, darling."
The desert is a voracious beast, devouring both flesh and stone.
Whether trained, ridden, or eaten, few goblin military innovations have rivaled the bug.
"Unimaginable riches? I assure you, I have a *vivid* imagination."
In the early days of Valley, desperate animalfolk harnessed the power of Calamity Beasts in ways that destroyed more than defended.
Jingling coins beckon many an eager hand.
Atarka serving-goblins coat themselves with grease imbued with noxious herbs, hoping to discourage their ravenous masters from adding them to the meal.
"This world will be ruled by its rightful sovereigns, not these hideous pretenders."
"Basically, we turn a bunch of little lightnings into one big lightning."
"Avacyn has abandoned us! We have nothing left except what we can take!"
What the initiates face in the final trial is completely at Hazoret's discretion.
"You burn. I'll pillage."
"Fire! Fire! Fire! What joy! What fire! Burn it all!"
The charge was heralded not by horns, but by the dragon's echoing roar.
Those with knowledge are wise to listen to those with imagination.
The Quicksilver Sea hissed and bubbled at the indignity. The Vulshok shaman just smiled.
"Glory to the Burning Ones! May their mighty fangs devour all foes!"
Ogres are driven by passion, rage, and another ogre standing behind them with a whip.
"Surely it won't notice if I take—" —Theria the Sly, last words
"Ready . . . uh . . . fire!"
A captured elemental makes for a potent, albeit unstable, power source.
Distant thunder rumbled, a dread forewarning of Keranos's displeasure.
The power of a waterfall. The fury of an avalanche. The intellect of a gale-force wind.
Attracting a dragon's attention may be the last mistake you make.
Her webs, spun from her own hair, reach from Nyx to the mortal world and even into the Underworld.
"We fight to stop a tyrant, but we also fight for the gentle creatures who have no concept of what befalls their world." —Vivien Reid
Only a worthy few are permitted within the sentient forest known as Axebane.
"Monsters dwell in every heart. We only think civilization tames them." —Euphemia, Nexus watcher
So-called "old wood" is rare in deforested Ravnica. Statues carved from it are said to house the last of the ancient nature spirits.
All seeds share a common bond, calling to each other across infinity.
"I want to help Zendikar. Show me the way." —Nissa Revane
"How truly vast this city must be, that I have traveled so far and seen so much, yet never once found the place where the buildings fail."
Emrakul does not grant wishes. Desires simply align to her will.
No spot in nature is truly barren.
On Murasa, even the trees grow trees.
"The land grows only where the kami will it." —Dosan the Falling Leaf
"Our enemy is nothing less than the end of all life. We shall not want for allies." —*The War Diaries*
Nature grows solutions to its problems.
There were no tombstones in orochi territory. Slain warriors were buried with a tree sapling, so they would become a part of the forest after death.
The first satyr to wake after a revel must search for the site of the next one.
"She speaks with the purity of nature and walks with the boldness of the wilds. She is a reminder of a world untamed." —Kamahl, druid acolyte
"New growth applies a healing poultice to wounds long scabbed over."
Those who enter the copse never leave. They find peace there and take root, becoming part of the ever-growing grove.
No one knew why the spiritmongers were so enraged by Phyrexian technology, but it was a stroke of good luck for the Coalition.
"We've been practicing for this all our lives. This is the final test!" —Korun Nar, Rubblebelt hunter
"Knock, knock."
Each flower identical, every leaf and petal disturbingly exact.
"Mana grows and changes like the roots of a plant. Like a plant, it must be nurtured." —Nissa Revane
Sorin had created Avacyn, so it was a cruelty beyond imagining, a pain beyond description, that it fell upon him to end her forever.
"He may look like my father, but the man I knew and loved is gone." —Danitha
"Her hunger knows no limit. Left unchecked, she would feast on all of Tarkir." —Yasova Dragonclaw
Liliana whispered to whatever consciousness Oketra and Bontu had left. "You are the gods. He is the usurper. You know what to do."
Dromoka's followers forsake blood ties so that they may join a greater family.
Prismari students dance in the tension between passion and perfection.
Its wide-reaching roots draw more than water.
To the Golgari, anything buried is treasure.
An Atarka dragon's exhale cooks what its inhale consumes.
"Just a nibble for now. I wouldn't want to ruin my appetite."
The forlorn cries of the dead combine to make its laugh.
"All matter, animate or not, rots when exposed to time. We merely speed up the process." —Ezoc, Golgari rot farmer
"I study bone because that's where truth dwells. One monster knucklebone is wiser than all that damp meat in your head."
She hears every voice from the swirling, whispering mist and swears to tell their stories.
"When all you have is a hammer, everything looks like a nail. I merely propose expanding our toolbox."
"To comprehend the full answer requires years of temporal study. In short, they were now never born in the first place." —Teferi
As Narset struggled to meditate, tiny dragonlings spiraled around her, conjuring thoughts of ancient clans.
The maze-like design embodies the core of Azorius law—strict structure designed to test wills and stall change.
Carved high into stone, the signet requires all to look up at it—whether with fear or admiration.
"The Northern Beacon flared, and even before the drawbridge finished its descent, the knights charged out." —*Legend of the Gilded Knights*
"What do you have that I cannot obtain?" —Mairsil, the Pretender
"Arise, great one, and cleanse the world of our enemies!"
The Izzet signet is redesigned often, each time becoming closer to a vanity portrait of Niv-Mizzet.
"Another failure," grumbled the toymaker. She slammed the door with such gusto that she failed to notice the eyes watching her.
The sigil holds different meanings depending on its form and presentation. While some wear it as a sign of status, others wear it as a sign of debt.
The symbol of the Conclave is one of unity, with tree supporting sun and sun feeding tree.
"There is great wisdom in rushing headlong into combat … if you're prepared." —Kenjek, captain of the Thousand Swords
"The sun banishes darkness every morning. I too will rise with such assuredness." —Huatli
"Good ideas don't take time. They take a lot of bad ideas first." —Ral Zarek
"You'll never get to the top if you don't know who's already there." —Kaya
Druids hold certain plants to be sacred and use their leaves and wood as a spellcasting focus.
Oriq agents stick to the dark corners of Arcavios, unseen yet ever-present.
Left barren by the Brothers' War, it stands as a stark reminder of Dominaria's likely fate should the Coalition fail.
"As Terisiare's mines ran dry, scrap metal became increasingly plentiful." —*The Antiquities War*
The continent of Murasa lies beneath a blanket of dense vegetation, its enormous branches tangled so thickly that some inhabitants never see the ground.
Travelers bathe in the falls to wash away curses from the pucas who lurk nearby.
Without Ardenvale's loyalty, the realm would greedily devour itself.
Without Embereth's courage, the realm would falter and fall.
After years of silence, the caves once again echo with the grisly sounds of Phyrexians preparing for war.
On the volcanic continent of Akoum, bizarre vegetation clusters around gas vents, and jagged mountain peaks rise high into the air.
The sunlight falls pristine on the temple at Epityr, softened by the remembered shadows of angelic saviors' wings.
"I gazed once into that light. Now it burns in my mind, forever denying me rest." —Riku of Two Reflections
The caves stretch farther than anyone knows, and the terrible legacy of Yawgmoth lurks in every shadow.
Murky Otarian tides hide the forgotten treacheries of the Phyrexian war.
Soothing whispers invite travelers to step closer, closer, closer . . . until they vanish soundlessly beneath the surface.
"This is it! All the cryptoliths point here!" —Jace Beleren
"It was a strange morning. When we awoke, we found our trees transformed. We didn't know whether to water them or polish them." —Pulan, Bant orchardist
Stability and volatility churn together, creating beauty and danger both.
"Do not linger in such places, child. There the gwyllions dance. If they find you, you will join in their revels for eternity." —Talara, elvish safewright
At full moon, the river seeps over its banks and crawls through the woods like a blanket of serpents.
Ships blown north in their voyage across the Stormwreck Sea become trapped in the unmelting ice.
Some of the nature spirits and wraiths that haunt Urborg take offense at the term "ghost town."
"Our ancestors brought down a Phyrexian portal ship, then built our town on its hull. We're pretty proud of that." —Alene of Riverspan
Serra's blessing lies strongest upon Sursi, where her holy chapels are untouched even as evil encroaches.
Between jagged, snowcapped peaks, the dense bands of hardy evergreens provide the perfect cover for roving bands of orc and goblin raiders.
When a werewolf changes for the first time, that first howl is said to echo through the wilds till moonset.
"The sylex blast marked not only the end of the war, but the end of Dominaria as most knew it." —*The Antiquities War*
Lush growth spreads like a ferocious blaze across the Otarian hillsides.
A few weed-choked gourd patches are all that remain of the proud, thriving farms that once blanketed the province.
The continent of Ondu is a vast plateau crisscrossed by deep trenches and meandering rivers.
Yavimaya's inhabitants are dedicated to protecting its unspoiled jungle from the scourge of artifice.
Once guarded by the Knights of the Reliquary, the tower stands now protected only by its own remoteness, its dusty treasures open to plunder by anyone.
Cries of panic echo along Kessig's narrow ravines as howlpacks herd their prey.
Cliffs echo and branches quake at the roar of life.
Hobs bury their kin far from home. They believe the dry, open ground keeps hags from stealing the bones and gwyllions from stealing the spirits.
The Quietus Cult holds their grim ceremonies in the dark places where unburied dead litter the ground.
The boiling seas around Shiv provided a welcome layer of protection for the reclaimed Mana Rig.
From Otaria, the sun above meets the sea below at a glittering horizon.
The continent of Guul Draz is a geothermal swampland reeking of heat and decay.
"We have inherited the mysteries of the Thran, but few of the answers." —Jhoira
On Otaria, peace and harmony are rare. Places that provide both are cherished.
On the continent of Tazeem, rushing waters plunge through narrow canyons into mist-cloaked lakes.
To the Sun Empire, any place where daylight brightens the jungle floor is sacred ground.
The House's geography constantly warps and twists, fields melting into floorboards and walls opening into hungry maws.
As their roots soaked in a weak tea of bogwater and decay, the trees absorbed the essence of death into their living tissue.
"For centuries my creation kept this world in balance. Now only her shadow remains." —Sorin Markov
"They never found the body of young Josu, or that of his murderous sister." —"The Fall of the House of Vess"
As magnigoth trees expanded across the sea into Almaaz and New Argive, it became clear Yavimaya's borders were never confined by its coastline.
